The color of a common crow is black.

The provided text explores the duality of interpretation in literature, specifically regarding Hemingway's *The Old Man and the Sea*. From one perspective, readers who emphasize the process and personal growth find inspiration in Santiago’s resilience, viewing his struggle as a triumph of the human spirit regardless of the material outcome. Conversely, readers who focus on tangible results and external validation may interpret the same events as a cautionary tale about the emptiness of effort when it does not yield a concrete reward. This contrast highlights how individual values and life experiences shape our understanding of narrative meaning, suggesting that a single text can simultaneously represent both heroic perseverance and tragic futility depending on the viewer's lens.
